6.1: The true renunciate is one who does what ought to be done without depending on the fruit — not one who merely gives up fire and rites.
6.2: Know renunciation to be yoga; no one becomes a yogi without abandoning selfish purpose.
6.3: For the one climbing, action is the means; for the one who has attained, serenity is the means.
6.4: When one is attached neither to sense objects nor to actions, having renounced all purpose, one is said to have attained yoga.
6.5: Lift yourself by yourself; do not degrade yourself — the self alone is the friend and the enemy of the self.
6.6: For one who has conquered the self, the self is a friend; for the unconquered, it behaves like an enemy.
6.7: The self-conquered and serene is steady in cold and heat, pleasure and pain, honour and dishonour.
6.8: Content with knowledge and realisation, unshaken, senses conquered, seeing a clod, a stone and gold alike — such a one is united.
6.9: Higher still: one who is even-minded towards friend, enemy, stranger, the hateful and the righteous alike.
6.10: Let the yogi constantly practise in solitude, alone, mind and body controlled, free of desire and possessions.
6.11: The practical instruction: a clean firm seat, neither too high nor too low, covered with cloth, skin and grass.
6.12: There, with mind one-pointed and thought and senses controlled, sit and practise yoga for self-purification.
6.13: Hold body, head and neck erect and still, gazing at the tip of the nose without looking around.
6.14: Serene, fearless, firm in the vow of celibacy, mind controlled and thinking of Me, sit intent on Me.
6.15: The yogi of controlled mind, ever practising, attains the peace that culminates in liberation and rests in Me.
6.16: Yoga is not for the one who eats too much or too little, nor for one who sleeps too much or too little.
6.17: For one moderate in food, recreation, work, sleep and waking, yoga becomes the destroyer of sorrow.
6.18: When the disciplined mind rests in the Self alone, free of longing for any desire, one is said to be united.
6.19: The famous image: as a lamp in a windless place does not flicker, so is the yogi of controlled mind.
6.20: Where the mind, restrained by yoga, comes to rest, and where seeing the Self by the self one is satisfied —
6.21: — there one knows the infinite joy grasped by the intellect and beyond the senses, and never moves from the truth.
6.22: Having gained it, one considers no other gain greater, and is not shaken even by heavy sorrow.
6.23: That severance from union with pain is called yoga; it should be practised with determination and an undespairing mind.
6.24: Abandoning without reserve all desires born of imagination, restraining the senses from every side —
6.25: — little by little let one withdraw, with intellect held firm; fixing the mind on the Self, think of nothing else.
6.26: Wherever the restless mind wanders, restrain it and bring it back under the control of the Self.
6.27: Supreme joy comes to the yogi whose mind is peaceful, passion quieted, sinless and become Brahman.
6.28: Ever engaged in yoga, freed from evil, the yogi easily enjoys the infinite bliss of contact with Brahman.
6.29: The yogi sees the Self in all beings and all beings in the Self, everywhere the same.
6.30: One who sees Me everywhere and sees all in Me — I am never lost to that one, nor is that one lost to Me.
6.31: The yogi established in unity, worshipping Me abiding in all beings, dwells in Me whatever the mode of life.
6.32: The highest yogi is one who judges pleasure and pain everywhere by the same standard as their own.
6.33: Arjuna's honest doubt: this yoga of evenness you describe — I do not see how it can last, because the mind is restless.
6.34: The mind is restless, turbulent, strong and obstinate; I think it as hard to control as the wind.
6.35: Krishna agrees it is hard, but says the mind is restrained by practice and dispassion.
6.36: Yoga is hard to attain for one whose self is uncontrolled, but attainable by the striving and self-controlled.
6.37: Arjuna's kindest question: what becomes of one who has faith but fails to control the mind and falls from yoga?
6.38: Does such a one perish like a riven cloud, supportless, fallen from both paths?
6.39: Please dispel this doubt completely; there is none other than you who can remove it.
6.40: Krishna's reassurance: there is no destruction here or hereafter — one who does good never comes to grief.
6.41: The fallen yogi attains the worlds of the righteous, dwells there for years, then is born in a pure and prosperous house.
6.42: Or is born in a family of wise yogis — though such a birth is very hard to obtain in this world.
6.43: There one regains the knowledge acquired in the former body and strives again for perfection.
6.44: By that former practice one is carried on irresistibly; even the seeker of yoga goes beyond ritual.
6.45: Striving diligently over many births, the yogi is purified of sin and reaches the supreme goal.
6.46: The yogi is greater than the ascetic, greater than the learned, greater than the ritualist — therefore be a yogi.
6.47: Of all yogis, the one who worships Me with faith, with the inner self merged in Me, is the most united.
